summary: Reviewed auth refactor and the accompanying plan. Two findings: a code-level date parser that silently drops DD/MM/YYYY input, and a plan-level gap where Phase 2 lacks error handling despite BC-AUTH-003 requiring graceful network failure. Both are concrete, reachable, and blocking.

findings.title: parseDate silently drops DD/MM/YYYY input
findings.what_wrong: Users submitting dates in DD/MM/YYYY hit a silent parse error that logs them out. parseDate only accepts YYYY-MM-DD and returns null; the caller at line 78 does not check the result and treats null as 'expired'.
findings.suggested_fix: Detect both formats explicitly; throw a typed error on unrecognized input so the caller routes to the retry dialog instead of logging the user out.
findings.evidence: src/auth.ts:42-55 shows the regex; src/auth.ts:78 shows the caller treating null as expired.

findings.title: Phase 2 network-failure fallback is missing despite BC-AUTH-003
findings.what_wrong: When the network request in Phase 2 fails, users will see a crash. The plan does not specify fallback UI or retry logic, and BC-AUTH-003 (graceful network failure) has no task claim.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a task under Phase 2 that claims BC-AUTH-003 and specifies the fallback UI plus exponential-backoff retry.
findings.evidence: docs/plans/refactor-rigor-gradient-pipeline.md Phase 2 tasks list; BC-AUTH-003 appears in behavioral_contract[] with zero fulfills claims.

residual_risks: Date format detection may still fail for ambiguous inputs like 01/02/2026 (is it Jan 2 or Feb 1?). Out of scope for this review but worth a follow-up.
